title: Introduction to Angular Forms 📝
description: Learn the two form approaches Angular provides and when to choose each.

slides.title: Why Forms Matter 🔑
slides.content:
# Forms Are Everywhere

Almost every web app needs user input: login, registration, search, settings.

Angular provides **two powerful ways** to build forms:

1. **Template‑Driven Forms** – logic lives in the template; simple and quick.
2. **Reactive Forms** – logic lives in the component class; more control and testability.

Both are fully featured with validation, change tracking, and data binding.

slides.title: Template‑Driven vs Reactive 🥊
slides.content:
| Feature | Template‑Driven | Reactive |
|---------|----------------|----------|
| Setup | `FormsModule` | `ReactiveFormsModule` |
| Form model | Implicit (created by directives) | Explicit (created in class) |
| Data flow | Two‑way binding (`[(ngModel)]`) | One‑way from model to view, events from view to model |
| Validation | Directives (e.g., `required`) | Functions / Validators class |
| Testing | Harder (logic in template) | Easier (logic in class) |
| Best for | Simple forms, prototypes | Complex forms, dynamic forms |

quizData.question: Which module is needed for template‑driven forms?

slides.title: When to Use Which? 🤔
slides.content:
Use **template‑driven** when:
* The form is simple (few fields).
* You prefer to keep logic in the template.
* You need rapid prototyping.

Use **reactive** when:
* The form is complex or dynamic (e.g., adding fields on the fly).
* You need unit‑testable form logic.
* You require custom validators that depend on multiple controls.

In a real app, you might use both for different parts.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Start Template‑Driven, Refactor to Reactive

For small forms, template‑driven is fast. As requirements grow, you can gradually migrate to reactive forms without rewriting the entire app.

slides.title: Don't Mix Modules in One Form ⚠️
slides.content: A single form should use either all template‑driven directives (`ngModel`) or reactive directives (`formControl`, `formGroup`). Mixing them can cause unpredictable behavior.
